blocks.h2: Where Pipes Freeze in Lincoln Park Buildings
blocks.body: In older Lincoln Park buildings, pipes freeze where heat doesn't reach: kitchen sinks on outside walls, enclosed back porches, unheated basements and pipes near drafty windows. In condo buildings, a vacant unit with the heat turned down can freeze and flood the units below. On the coldest nights, keep the heat steady, open cabinet doors on outside walls and let a faucet drip.

blocks.h2: Frozen Pipe Questions From Lincoln Park Homeowners

items.q: My kitchen faucet is frozen. What should I do?
items.preview: Open the cabinet, open the faucet and warm the pipe gently.
items.answer: Open the cabinet doors, open the faucet and warm the pipe with a hair dryer. Never use a flame. If it doesn't thaw, call us.

items.q: How can I keep pipes from freezing in an older building?
items.preview: Heat, open cabinets and a slow drip.
items.answer: Keep the heat up, open cabinets on exterior walls and let a faucet drip on the coldest nights.

items.q: Can you repair a pipe inside a shared wall?
items.answer: Yes. We locate the break and open only what we need.
Often. Check with your agent or association.

items.q: My upstairs neighbor is away and I hear water. What do I do?
items.preview: Contact the building and call us.
items.answer: Contact the association or building contact right away and call us. Shutting off the main may be needed.

items.q: How much does burst pipe repair cost in Lincoln Park?
items.preview: It depends on the break. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on where the pipe burst and how we reach it. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
